title: TransFusion: End-to-End Transformer Acceleration via Graph Fusion and Pipelining
problem: Transformer acceleration has focused on fusing individual submodules (MHA, softmax) in isolation, but as models grow in depth and context length, inter-layer data movement, buffer fragmentation, and scheduling inefficiencies across the full encoder/decoder stack (QKV projections, MHA, LayerNorm, FFN) dominate end-to-end latency and cannot be addressed by fragmented per-module optimizations.
method: TransFusion represents the full Transformer layer stack as Einsum Cascades — a structured DAG of Einsum operations capturing precise data dependencies and execution order. The DPipe scheduler partitions this Einsum DAG and applies latency-aware inter-layer pipelining across hardware memory hierarchies using dynamic programming to balance FFN and attention stages. TileSeek, a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based tiling search algorithm, explores the tile configuration space to balance buffer reuse against on-chip memory constraints at both cloud and edge scales.

title: FAST: An FHE Accelerator for Scalable-parallelism with Tunable-bit
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) imposes enormous computational overhead compared to plaintext computation, and existing FHE accelerators do not exploit recent cryptographic optimizations—specifically hoisting technology and the gadget decomposition key-switching (KLSS) method—leaving significant performance on the table. Additionally, ciphertext level consumption varies significantly during application execution, causing workload imbalance that accelerators with fixed precision do not address.
method: FAST is an FHE accelerator that integrates hoisting technology (reducing redundant NTT operations in key-switching) and the KLSS gadget decomposition key-switching method. A versatile framework supports both hybrid and KLSS key-switching within a single application execution, dynamically adapting to varying ciphertext levels. The accelerator implements tunable-bit arithmetic to match the differing computational precision requirements of hybrid vs. KLSS key-switching at different ciphertext levels. Scalable parallelism is achieved through a configurable array of processing elements that can be provisioned to match the current workload's level and method requirements.

title: Engine-Agnostic Model Hot-Swapping for Cost-Effective LLM Inference
problem: LLM inference services face cost/efficiency challenges: GPUs must handle bursty requests, leading to underutilization and high costs; models must be swapped between GPU and host memory.
method: SwapServeLLM: engine-agnostic hot-swapping using GPU checkpointing. Mechanisms: (1) demand-aware preemption via concurrent request info, (2) memory-aware routing with minimized latency.

title: 23.7 BROCA: A 52.4-to-559.2mW Mobile Social Agent System-on-Chip with Adaptive Bit-Truncate Unit and Acoustic-Cluster Bit Grouping
problem: On-device conversational AI requires integrating multimodal perception (speech/vision), retrieval-augmented generation, language modeling, emotion generation, and voice synthesis in power-constrained mobile devices while maintaining quality.
method: BROCA SoC integrates four-stage pipeline: user perception (multimodal encoder), retrieval-augmented generation, response generation (transformer language model), emotion generation, and agent feedback (vocoder); adaptive bit-truncation and acoustic-cluster bit grouping optimize precision per module for power efficiency.

title: EMLIO: Minimizing I/O Latency and Energy Consumption for Large-Scale AI Training
problem: Large-scale deep learning training faces I/O bottlenecks as datasets exceed local storage and GPU compute outpaces network/disk latencies. While recent systems optimize data-loading time, energy consumption of I/O—critical at scale—is overlooked. Multi-environment networks (LAN/WAN) require different strategies.
method: EMLIO: Efficient ML I/O service. Deploys lightweight daemon on storage nodes that serializes/batches raw samples, streams over TCP with out-of-order prefetching. Integrates with GPU preprocessing (NVIDIA DALI) on client. Evaluates across local disk, LAN (0.05ms, 10ms RTT), WAN (30ms RTT).

title: Clearance-Constrained PCB Global Placement with Heterogeneous Components
problem: PCB placement must handle pad-to-pad clearance constraints and heterogeneous components while minimizing routing congestion and overlap.
method: PCB placement framework with: wire-area model accounting for routing resource needs (power/signal nets); pad-to-pad clearance model; two-sided density model for component and pad overlap; quadratic programming-based legalizer resolving violations.

title: Complex Parsing for In-Network Acceleration of High-Energy Physics Experiments
problem: High-Energy Physics (HEP) experiments like DUNE generate massive volumes of network traffic with custom packet formats. Processing this data at the compute layer creates bottlenecks. In-network processing on programmable switches could offload parsing.
method: Implements custom packet parser for DUNE protocol on Tofino programmable network switch. Deployed on FABRIC testbed. Uses network traffic generated by ICEBERG DUNE prototype detector. Evaluates feasibility, performance bottlenecks, and identifies techniques for overcoming parsing challenges.

title: Optimizing Recovery Logic in Speculative High-Level Synthesis
problem: Speculative HLS introduces significant area overhead from rollback control logic when handling kernels with complex, irregular control-flow, offsetting throughput gains.
method: Combines static analysis and linear programming to simplify and eliminate unnecessary rollback logic. The approach identifies which speculation paths require rollback handling and optimizes the control logic structure accordingly.

title: SMX: Heterogeneous Architecture for Universal Sequence Alignment Acceleration
problem: Sequence alignment accelerators are over-specialized to one alignment model (e.g., Smith-Waterman with affine gaps or simple substitution matrices) and fail to support the full variety of irregular use cases in practice (DNA, protein, ASCII text; weighted gaps; diverse substitution matrices), while general-purpose CPUs and GPUs lack the efficiency of domain-specific designs.
method: SMX is a heterogeneous architecture that integrates two components orchestrated by a general-purpose core: an ISA extension (SMX-1D) for irregular and sequential alignment tasks, and a specialized 2D coprocessor (SMX-2D) to accelerate the regular, parallel compute-intensive phases of dynamic programming. The ISA extension adds new instructions to handle variable-length sequences and edge cases, while the coprocessor accelerates the systolic-style inner-loop wavefront computation. Both components support multiple sequence types (DNA, protein, ASCII) and alignment models including weighted affine gap penalties and full substitution matrices, enabling seamless integration with state-of-the-art software alignment algorithms. Physical design targets a 22nm technology node with an area of 0.34mm², 30% of a single-issue in-order CPU core.

title: 16.3 An on-Device Generative AI Focused Neural Processing Unit in 4nm Flagship Mobile SoC with Fan-Out Wafer-Level Package
problem: On-device generative AI (LLMs like LLaMA, visual models like Stable Diffusion) exhibit fundamentally different computational characteristics than traditional CNNs: LLMs are memory-intensive with streaming weight reads (GB per token), while visual models are compute-intensive with softmax/layernorm dominating (40% of ops vs. 90-99% for conv in CNNs), requiring heterogeneous compute architecture.
method: Heterogeneous NPU with vector engines and dual tensor engines: one optimized for memory-intensive sequential operations (LLM inference with weight streaming), another for compute-intensive matrix operations (vision models). Memory hierarchy with on-chip/DRAM tiling enables efficient weight caching. Fan-out wafer-level package (FOWLP) improves thermal dissipation enabling sustained high performance. 4nm Samsung Exynos 2400 integration achieves broad neural network support across CNNs, LLMs, and visual models.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper TurboFNO: High-Performance Fourier Neural Operator with Fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT on GPU
problem: Reproducibility report meta-paper: evaluation of artifact reproducibility for TurboFNO paper (full paper analysis not available from abstract)
method: Artifact evaluation conducted by SC25 Reproducibility Committee member, assessing the Artifact Description and Evaluation appendix of the TurboFNO paper.

title: 32.1 A 180MHz 45.3%-Peak-Efficiency Isolated Converter Using Q-Downsize Class-D Power Amplifier with Inherent Shoot-Through Current Blocking and High Tolerance for Efficiency Despite Frequency Misalignments
problem: Isolated DC-DC converters suffer from high electromagnetic interference (EMI) due to common-mode (CM) current across the isolation barrier; suppressing CM voltage variation requires fully symmetrical transmitter (TX) topologies but introduces complexity.
method: Class-D power amplifier with Q-downsize technique that inherently blocks shoot-through current, combined with fully symmetrical TX topology and coil routing in opposite directions to cancel magnetic field, achieving 45.3% peak efficiency at 180MHz with high tolerance to frequency variations.

title: Velosiraptor: Code Synthesis for Memory Translation
problem: OS code for configuring hardware memory translation and protection mechanisms must be manually adapted for each new hardware design, a repetitive and error-prone process that can introduce security-critical bugs breaking isolation guarantees for untrusted applications.
method: Velosiraptor synthesizes correct-by-construction OS memory translation code from a hardware-description specification of the translation/protection hardware. It takes a formal hardware model (specifying translation table formats, field semantics, and configuration operations) as input and automatically generates the OS driver code that correctly configures the hardware. The synthesis process uses a component library of translation operations and a constraint solver or template-based code generator to produce verified, hardware-specific configuration routines without manual coding.

title: A 14-nm Energy-Efficient and Reconfigurable Analog Current-Domain In-Memory Compute SRAM Accelerator
problem: This work presents a low-power reconfigurable 12T-SRAM current-domain analog in-memory computing (IMC) SRAM macro design to address non-linearities, process variations, and limited throughput
method: proposed design features a time-domain subthreshold multiply and accumulate (MAC) operation with a differential output current sensing technique

title: PICK: An SRAM-based Processing-in-Memory Accelerator for K-Nearest-Neighbor Search in Point Clouds
problem: K-nearest neighbor (kNN) search on point clouds is computationally intense and memory-heavy, but off-chip memory access dominates latency and energy. Current approaches struggle with resource-constrained scenarios typical in edge AI and autonomous driving.
method: PICK is a PIM (processing-in-memory) architecture using bit-serial PIM (BS-PIM) to perform kNN search with on-chip SRAM, eliminating off-chip access. Includes: (1) bit-width clipping for bit-serial distance calculation with reduced latency; (2) filtering-and-selection strategy achieving approximately constant time for arbitrary k; (3) two-stage pipeline parallelizing distance calculation and top-k selection.

title: Profiling Application-Specific Properties of Irregular Graph Algorithms on GPUs
problem: Despite sophisticated GPU profiling tools (NVIDIA Nsight Compute/Systems), developers often miss application-specific insights that simple manual profiling techniques can reveal, particularly for irregular workloads like graph algorithms.
method: Demonstrate manual profiling approach using source code instrumentation on five high-performance GPU graph analytics codes. Show how analysis of global and thread-local counters reveals application-specific behavior, validates assumptions, and guides targeted optimizations.
